Good morning, excellencies, distinguished delegates.
It is my pleasure to welcome you to the second regular session of the UN Women Executive Board.
I'm pleased to welcome you all and the following UN colleagues who will be on the podium.
Ms. Sima Bahous, Under-Secretary-General and Executive Director.
Ms. Nyaradzayi Gumbozvanda, Assistant Secretary-General and Deputy Executive Director for Normative Support, UN System Coordination and Programme Results.
Mr. Mohammad Nasiri, Chief of Staff.
Mr. Kambou, for Fana, Chief Financial Officer and Director of the Division of Finance and Administration.
Ms. Anna Kaffine Jatfos, Director, Strategic Planning, Results and Effectiveness Division.
Ms. Sarah Hendrix, Director, Policy, Program and Intergovernmental Division.
and last but not least, Mr. Jhalok Boris, Secretary of the Executive Board.
The annotated provision agenda and work program for the second regular session was shared with all the members.
Agenda item one, we shall have organizational matters for the adoption of the annotated provisional agenda and work programme for the current session and the report of the annual session of 2026.
For the adoption of the annotated provisional agenda and work programme for the current session, I now invite the Secretary of the Board, Mr. Jalok Boris, to outline the agenda of today's session.
Mr. Secretary, you have the floor.
Thank you very much.
Mr. President, good morning.
Distinguished delegates, very good morning to you all.

So following the adoption of the provisional agenda and work plan for this session, as well as the adoption of the report on the annual session earlier this year, This session will continue with official opening statements by you, Mr. President, followed by the statement of our Executive Director.

Before opening the floor to Member States, the Executive Board will turn to agenda item 2 on UNAT and receive a short presentation from our Chief of Staff on UN Women's engagement with UNAT initiative, including additional information on the alternative options.

topics.label: UN System Reform and Institutional Options
topics.description: A central discussion focused on the UN80 reform process, especially whether closer alignment or a possible merger between UN Women and UNFPA would improve effectiveness, coherence, and efficiency. Many speakers stressed that any reform must be evidence-based, member state-led, transparent, and judged by its impact on women and girls.

sentences.text: Then the floor will be open for Member States to deliver their opening statements, managed through a speakers list circulated yesterday.
By the way, the speakers list is pretty long today.
We have about 40 names on the list, and so we will unfortunately cut the mics after three minutes for national statement and five minutes for group statements.

00 p.m., the Executive Board will adjourn the morning session and reserve the following couple of hours for informal consultation on draft decision in Conference Room A. The Executive Board will resume the plenary at 3:00 p.m. in this room to discuss item 3 on structured dialogue on financing, where we will discuss the report on the structured dialogue on financing, the result of the strategic plan.

sentences.text: Once this item has been concluded, the plenary meeting will be adjourned, with negotiation resuming on the draft decision, and that will happen at the UN Women headquarters.

The plenary meeting will then resume tomorrow, the second day, Wednesday, the 10th of September, 00 a.m. with agenda item 4 on the GIU review of governance and oversight of the executive boards of UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS, UNICEF and UN Women, and receive an update on the progress made on this front.

sentences.text: After that, the Executive Board will turn to agenda item 5, other matters, to take action on the draft decisions, and then we'll return to agenda item 1, organizational matters, whereby we will approve the provisional agenda and work plan for the first regular session 2027 and the annual work plan of the Executive Board for 2027.
The second regular session will conclude with closing statements, as always, by you, Mr. President, and the Executive Director of UN Women.
Before concluding, I would like to bring your attention on the screen.
You can see that we are tweeting regularly on the proceeding of the Executive Board.
Please follow us at UN Women Board, as it's shown on the screen.
Thank you very much, Mr. President.
Thank you, Mr. Secretary. May I take it that the Executive Board now wishes to adopt the annotated provisional agenda and work plan for the second regular session 2026?
I see no objections, so decided.
Thank you.
The agenda and work plan as adopted will guide us for the rest of this session.
Let us now turn to the adoption of the report of the annual session 2026.
May I take it that the Executive Board wishes to adopt the report of the previous session?
I see no objections.
So decided.
Then it is now my pleasure to turn to the official opening of this session.
Excellencies, these are my remarks as President.
Excellencies, distinguished delegates and colleagues, I'm very pleased to welcome you to this year's second regular session of the UN Women Executive Board.
I look forward to two rewarding days of discussion and consultation as we stay on course and work to fulfill UN Women's triple mandate.
Please note that the second regular session adheres to the code of conduct to prevent harassment, including sexual harassment, at UN system events.
This document is of integral importance to ensure the safety of all personnel and participants during our events, including the Executive Board.
You can access the code of conduct online.

I would like to extend a warm welcome to Executive Director Ms. Shimma Mahauz on behalf of the Bureau and all Member States, and congratulate her on nearing, or approaching, almost five years in office.
Excellencies, distinguished colleagues, throughout this session, we have before us several important reports and briefs.
including the update on UN Women's engagement with the UN80 Initiative.

We also look forward to the presentation of the official report on the structured dialogue on financing the results of the UN Women Strategic Plan 2022-2025, as well as receiving an update on the progress made regarding the JIU review of governance and oversight of the Executive Boards of UNDP/UNFPA/UNOPS, UNICEF and UN Women.
The oversight and policy guidance of the Executive Board would not be complete without actionable outcomes to our Executive Board official meetings.

We have before us three draft decisions: Decision 2026/16 on the report of the structured dialogue on financing the results of the UN Women Strategic Plan 2022-2025 and the future direction for the Strategic Plan 2026-2029.
Second, decision 2026/17 on JIU review of governance and oversight of the Executive Boards of UNDP/UNFPA/UNHCR.
UNOPS, UNICEF, and UN Women.
And another decision, 2026/17, on engagement with the UN80 Initiative.

I would like to extend my gratitude to the delegations from Albania, Belgium, and my own country, Uganda, for their facilitation of these decisions, and the Secretariat for supporting these negotiations.
I call upon our delegations to demonstrate flexibility and understanding during these discussions, enabling us to reach consensus on these outcomes.

I would also like to acknowledge the diligent efforts of UN Women colleagues, Patricio, the Executive Board Secretary, and his team, for the organization of this session, and the informal briefings leading up to the session.
I trust in the continued support of the Board in maximizing our negotiations on time, and I expect a successful culmination of the event.
At this juncture, I'm delighted to pass the floor to the Executive Director for her opening statement.
Madam Executive Director, I give you the floor.
Thank you, Mr. President, Excellencies, distinguished members of the Executive Board.
Good morning to you all.
I thank His Excellency Godfrey Kuyaba, Ambassador at the Permanent Mission of Uganda, for presiding over our Executive Board this morning and for his stewardship and steadfast support.

My appreciation also to the Bureau members, Her Excellency Ambassador Suella Janina of Albania, Her Excellency Ambassador Sophie de Smet of Belgium, Her Excellency Ambassador Aida Kazimlieva of Kyrgyzstan, and serving formally for the Latin American and Caribbean Group, Her Excellency Alejandra Hernandez of the Dominican Republic.
Mr. President, allow me to begin on a positive note by celebrating progress made towards gender equality.
Last year brought renewed commitment to the Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action.
and gains for women and girls.
Member states adopted or amended 69 laws advancing gender equality.
52 countries established formal care systems, and women peacebuilders participated in every UN-led peace process.
